_jevModel: Pinned so a new Jev release can't move routes before eval/run.ts has run on it. Bump it, run the eval, then ship.
_upwardMass: When the tasks on a stronger model together hold at least this much of Jev's probability, the route takes that model even if a cheaper task was likelier. A route too low costs quality and one too high only money, so moving up needs less than winning does.
_pricing: USD per million tokens. cacheWrite is the 1-hour rate (2x input), which Claude Code sessions use; Haiku's cache prices are assumed at 0.1x / 2x input. Haiku charges its longContext rates once a request carries over 100K tokens. Check the pricing page and edit.
_switching: A step down to a cheaper model happens only when it saves `margin` times what the switch costs: the cheaper model writing the whole conversation into its cache, and the stronger one doing it again on the way back if its cache expired. The expected figures stand in until the session has turns of its own.
_guards: pushback: a prompt this matches (blunt openers like "no" or "wrong" at the start of the prompt, softer corrections like "I'm talking about..." or "it still doesn't work" at the start of any sentence, after at most two interjections like "ok," or "try again,"; a few phrases like "you're confusing me" anywhere) escalates the next holdTurns prompts a tier above the turn it answers. toolErrors: that many failed tool calls in one turn below the top model move the rest of it up a tier. followUp: a prompt this matches whole keeps the route in force without asking the classifier. events: a prompt the harness wrote rather than the person (a `!` command's output, a side session's or a background task's note) keeps the route in force too; a CI event or another session's message asks for a job, so it is classified.

_tasks: The classifier names one of these. Each runs on at least its model and effort; the classifier's effort can raise it, never lower it. `not` marks where a task ends. A task with `raiseAbove` is asked about on its own, yes or no, and raises whatever task was named when Jev's chance of yes reaches it. Jev leans slightly toward the first option listed, so the cheap tasks go last: a lean costs money, not quality.

tasks.name: risky
tasks.when: A mistake in this job would be costly or hard to undo: changing security, auth, secrets or permissions; payments or billing; migrating, overwriting or deleting data; deploying to production or changing live infrastructure; concurrency.
tasks.not: Nothing here is costly to get wrong or hard to undo: local edits that version control can undo, work on a feature branch, opening a pull request, sending a message, archiving or tidying sessions, moving local files, reading or reporting without changing anything.

tasks.name: debug
tasks.when: Finding the cause of a failure nobody understands yet: a flaky or failing test with no obvious reason, a wrong result, a crash, a slow path, behaviour that differs between environments.
tasks.not: A failure whose cause is already known or stated in the request.

tasks.name: design
tasks.when: Deciding how something should be built or changed: architecture, a plan, a refactor across many files or systems, weighing approaches, open-ended research, orchestrating several agents.

tasks.name: review
tasks.when: Checking work rather than doing it: reviewing a diff or file for bugs, verifying a change does what it should, judging whether tests cover enough.

tasks.name: build
tasks.when: Writing or extending code or documents to a clear goal: a well-specified feature, script or test, fixing a bug whose cause is known or obvious, a refactor within a few files, a commit or PR description, writing up or updating a document from what has been discussed.
tasks.not: An open-ended aim with no known way to reach it, such as making something faster or more reliable, which first needs finding where the problem is.

tasks.name: lookup
tasks.when: Finding or reading things with no judgement about what to change: searching the code, reading or summarising a file or doc, running a command and reporting what it printed.

tasks.name: answer
tasks.when: A question with a direct answer and nothing to change: how something works, what a command, flag or error message means, a factual or how-do-I question.
tasks.not: A question of whether something is safe, correct or could go wrong, which needs checking.

tasks.name: mechanical
tasks.when: A small edit or action whose content the request fully dictates: a rename, a typo, formatting, a version bump, a one-line change spelled out in the request, a routine git or housekeeping command named in the request.
tasks.not: Anything where the assistant decides what to write: rewriting a document, applying what was discussed earlier, an edit alongside other work.

_models: Weakest first. maxContext is the most context, in tokens, a model is trusted to work in; past it the router keeps a stronger one.

efforts.name: low
efforts.when: The answer or edit is immediate; there is nothing to weigh or plan.

efforts.name: medium
efforts.when: A handful of steps carried out in an obvious order, with little to decide along the way.

efforts.name: high
efforts.when: Several interacting parts or trade-offs to think through before acting, or a cause that has to be investigated first.

efforts.name: xhigh
efforts.when: A hard, ambiguous or high-stakes problem where many possibilities must be explored and the result carefully verified.
